title: A bill to require entities to include human-controlled shutdown mechanisms in all artificial intelligence systems.
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: The bill requires companies and organizations that create or use artificial intelligence to build a human‑controlled shutdown mechanism into every system. This measure aims to give people the ability to quickly stop AI if it behaves unexpectedly, thereby improving safety and reducing risk.

title: To require the Secretary of Veterans Affairs to disclose each instance in which the Secretary uses artificial intelligence to interact with a covered individual, and for other purposes.
action: Referred to the House Committee on Veterans' Affairs.
summary: The policy requires the Secretary of Veterans Affairs to disclose every instance in which artificial intelligence is used to interact with a covered individual, as well as any other relevant applications. This requirement aims to increase transparency and accountability for AI use within VA services.

title: Stop Rogue AI Act
action: Referred to the Committee on Science, Space, and Technology, and in addition to the Committee on Oversight and Government Reform, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Stop Rogue AI Act is a proposed law designed to prevent artificial intelligence systems from acting in harmful or unauthorized ways. It would set up legal safeguards, oversight rules, and penalties to keep AI under strict human control and stop it from becoming rogue.

title: Open-Source AI Leadership Act
action: Forwarded by Subcommittee to Full Committee by Voice Vote.
summary: The Open-Source AI Leadership Act is a proposed law that encourages the use and development of open-source software in the field of artificial intelligence, aiming to increase collaboration and transparency among researchers and developers. It seeks to create standards, provide funding, and establish governance frameworks that support open AI projects and prevent a few companies from dominating the technology.

title: No AI Data Centers on Federal Lands Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on Natural Resources.
summary: The No AI Data Centers on Federal Lands Act prohibits the construction and operation of AI data centers on lands owned or managed by the federal government. It seeks to protect federal resources and prevent potential environmental and security impacts associated with such facilities.

title: Protecting Families from AI Data Center Energy Costs Act
action: Ordered to be Reported by the Yeas and Nays: 44 - 0.
summary: The Protecting Families from AI Data Center Energy Costs Act aims to shield households from the rising electric bills caused by large AI data centers. It proposes measures such as limiting energy usage, requiring cost‑sharing or rebates, and enforcing transparency to keep families’ energy costs affordable.

title: Stop AI Price Gouging and Wage Fixing Act of 2025
action: Referred to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, and in addition to the Committees on the Judiciary, and Education and Workforce, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Stop AI Price Gouging and Wage Fixing Act of 2025 is designed to curb the use of artificial intelligence for charging excessive prices and manipulating labor wages. It establishes rules that prohibit AI-driven price gouging and wage fixing, promoting fair market practices and protecting consumers and workers from AI-enabled exploitation.

title: Artificial Intelligence Data Center Moratorium Act
action: Referred to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, and in addition to the Committee on Foreign Affairs, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Data Center Moratorium Act proposes temporarily halting the construction and operation of new AI data centers. This pause is intended to allow policymakers to assess the environmental, economic, and societal impacts of such facilities before allowing them to resume.

title: To better coordinate Federal efforts to utilize advance technologies, such as artificial intelligence, to improve diagnoses, treatments, cures, and prevention strategies for pediatric cancer, and for other purposes.
action: Referred to the House Committee on Energy and Commerce.
summary: This policy aims to strengthen federal coordination in using advanced technologies, especially AI, to improve the diagnosis, treatment, cure, and prevention of pediatric cancer. It also covers broader uses of these technologies for other purposes beyond pediatric oncology.

title: Research and Oversight of AI in Courts Act of 2026
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on the Judiciary.
summary: The Research and Oversight of AI in Courts Act of 2026 establishes a framework for monitoring and evaluating the use of artificial intelligence technologies in the judicial system. It creates an independent oversight body that conducts research, publishes findings, and sets guidelines to ensure fairness, transparency, and accountability in AI‑assisted court proceedings.

title: Expressing the sense of the House of Representatives that every American and community impacted by the construction or operation of an artificial intelligence data center should have the right to transparency and local autonomy.
action: Referred to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, and in addition to the Committee on the Judiciary, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The House of Representatives has stated that any American and community affected by the construction or operation of an artificial intelligence data center should have the right to transparency and local autonomy. This means they must be fully informed and able to influence decisions that impact their area.

title: Deterring American AI Model Theft Act of 2026
action: Ordered to be Reported (Amended) by the Yeas and Nays: 43 - 0.
summary: The Deterring American AI Model Theft Act of 2026 seeks to protect AI developers by making it illegal to steal or unauthorizedly use AI models. It sets penalties and enforcement tools to discourage theft and encourage secure, responsible handling of AI technology.

title: Algorithmic Accountability Act of 2025
action: Referred to the House Committee on Energy and Commerce.
summary: The Algorithmic Accountability Act of 2025 would require companies that use automated decision systems to test for bias, errors, and fairness, and to share those findings with regulators. It would also give regulators the power to enforce corrections and protect consumers from unfair algorithmic decisions.

title: Protect Elections from Deceptive AI Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on House Administration.
summary: The Protect Elections from Deceptive AI Act aims to safeguard electoral integrity by regulating the use of deceptive AI tools and ensuring transparency in AI‑generated content. It establishes guidelines for political campaigns, imposes disclosure requirements, and creates enforcement mechanisms to detect and counteract AI‑driven misinformation targeting voters.

title: Homestake AI Act of 2026
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Energy and Natural Resources.
summary: The Homestake AI Act of 2026 establishes a framework for the responsible development and use of artificial intelligence, setting standards for safety, transparency, and accountability. It requires companies to register AI systems, conduct risk assessments, and ensures compliance with privacy laws and public oversight mechanisms.

title: A concurrent resolution expressing the sense of Congress that the Ratepayer Protection Pledge announced on March 4, 2026, reflects sound national policy to protect ratepayers in the United States, promote electricity affordability, and ensure that all people of the United States, including households, small businesses, schools, hospitals, and farms, have access to reliable and affordable energy as artificial intelligence and data center infrastructure expands across the United States.
action: Referred to the Committee on Energy and Natural Resources. (text: CR S1618-1619)
summary: This resolution states that Congress supports the Ratepayer Protection Pledge, which aims to safeguard consumers and keep electricity prices reasonable as AI and data‑center growth expands across the U.S. It emphasizes that everyone—households, small businesses, schools, hospitals, and farms—should have reliable and affordable energy.

title: Liquid Cooling for AI Act of 2025
action: Committee on Energy and Natural Resources Subcommittee on Energy. Hearings held. With printed Hearing: S.Hrg. 119-366.
summary: The Liquid Cooling for AI Act of 2025 establishes regulations to encourage the adoption of liquid‑cooling systems in AI data centers, aiming to improve energy efficiency and reduce heat output. It also sets safety standards, certification requirements, and incentives for operators to transition to liquid‑cooled infrastructure.

title: Artificial Intelligence Environmental Impacts Act of 2026
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Environment and Public Works.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Environmental Impacts Act of 2026 aims to reduce the ecological footprint of AI technologies by establishing guidelines for energy use, carbon emissions, and responsible data center design. It requires companies to assess and disclose the environmental impacts of their AI systems, encouraging greener practices and compliance with sustainability standards.

title: PROACTIV Artificial Intelligence Data Act of 2025
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: The PROACTIV Artificial Intelligence Data Act of 2025 is a proposed law that seeks to regulate the collection, use, and sharing of data for AI systems, ensuring privacy, security, and transparency. It establishes accountability standards, requires clear user consent, and aims to protect individuals while promoting responsible AI innovation.

title: Algorithmic Accountability Act of 2025
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: The Algorithmic Accountability Act of 2025 would require companies to conduct risk assessments for automated decision‑making systems to identify potential biases or harmful effects. It would also mandate transparency reporting and create oversight mechanisms to ensure fair and accountable use of AI.

title: Children's Artificial Intelligence Toy Safety Act of 2026
action: Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation. Ordered to be reported with an amendment in the nature of a substitute favorably.
summary: The Children's Artificial Intelligence Toy Safety Act of 2026 establishes strict safety standards for AI-powered toys sold to children, ensuring they are free from harmful behaviors and secure from data misuse. It requires manufacturers to conduct comprehensive safety testing, provide transparent usage information, and comply with ongoing regulatory oversight to protect young users.

title: Youth AI Privacy Act
action: Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation. Ordered to be reported with an amendment in the nature of a substitute favorably.
summary: The Youth AI Privacy Act is a law designed to protect the privacy of young people who use artificial intelligence. It sets strict rules about how data about minors can be collected, stored, and shared by companies that offer AI services.

title: Artificial Intelligence Physical Systems Coordination Act of 2026
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Physical Systems Coordination Act of 2026 establishes a federal framework for regulating and coordinating the deployment of AI-driven physical systems such as robots, drones, and autonomous vehicles. It aims to ensure safety, interoperability, and public accountability by creating oversight bodies and setting technical standards for these systems.

title: Expanding AI Voices Act
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: The Expanding AI Voices Act aims to broaden the range of perspectives represented in artificial intelligence systems. It seeks to promote inclusivity by encouraging diverse data sources and stakeholder participation in AI development.

title: Artificial Intelligence Data Center Moratorium Act
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Data Center Moratorium Act proposes a temporary halt on building new AI data centers. It aims to address environmental concerns and encourage more sustainable practices in the AI industry.
